The discharge headlight is a headlight that uses an HID bulb (high intensity discharge lamp) as its light source.

The light emitted from the HID bulb is a natural daylight color close to sunlight and illuminates a wider and more distant area ahead, helping to improve driver visibility; in addition, its low power consumption reduces the load on the battery and the bulb has a long service life.

The discharge headlight achieves instant lighting of the HID bulb and a stable power supply, and has a compact, lightweight light control computer; it is also combined with an automatic leveling function that keeps the vertical beam axis constant as a device to prevent dazzling oncoming vehicles.

The arc tube of the HID bulb is filled with a rare gas (xenon gas) and metal iodides (zinc, sodium and scandium), and arc discharge occurs in the arc tube due to the voltage applied to the base side and lead wire side.
UV-cut glass that absorbs ultraviolet rays is used for the outer tube of the arc tube, keeping ultraviolet radiation to a level equivalent to that of halogen bulbs.
The light control computer is a device that supplies the alternating current (AC) power required to illuminate the HID bulb.

The frequency of the AC power is several hundred Hz or more so that no flicker is perceived during illumination, and electromagnetic shielding is provided so that electromagnetic waves do not affect the vehicle radio, etc.

The light control computer achieves instant and stable illumination of the HID bulb through controls such as generating a high voltage of up to approximately 22,000V. Since this device generates high voltage, various fail-safe functions are incorporated, and consideration has also been given to ensuring reliability against heat, humidity, vibration, etc.

ENTRY.PTXT: 1. The battery voltage is converted into a high-voltage pulse (approximately 22,000V) by the light control computer in the lamp.
2. The high-voltage pulse is applied between both electrodes of the bulb, causing the xenon gas to emit light.
3. Arc discharge occurs as the temperature inside the bulb rises.
4. As the temperature rises further, the metal iodide vaporizes and separates, and the metal atoms emit light by discharge.
5. The light control computer optimally controls the power supplied to the bulb.

MECA.TITLE: Fail-safe Function of Light Control Computer

ITEM.PTXT: When a malfunction occurs in the output voltage, input voltage or lamp side voltage, the light control computer performs fail-safe as follows.

ENTRY.PTXT: When an output malfunction is detected (short, open or leak detected) and when the bulb flickers

If a malfunction occurs in the output voltage or bulb flickering continues for 60 +/- 20 seconds or more, the headlight is turned off and remains in that state until the power is turned on again (headlight switch OFF → ON or power switch (IG) OFF → ON).

If the input voltage is outside the operating voltage (10 to 16V), the headlight is turned off, and it illuminates again as soon as the input returns to the operating range. However, if the input voltage drops after illumination, the headlight remains illuminated until the voltage reaches the illumination holding limit voltage (6V or less).
If a lamp voltage malfunction is detected, the headlight is turned off and remains in that state until the power is turned on again (headlight switch OFF → ON or power switch (IG) OFF → ON).

According to the status signal of the headlight leveling switch in the cabin (level 0 for the uppermost direction, level 5 for the lowermost direction), the headlight leveling actuators are driven to move the reflectors up and down and change the direction of the beam axis.

Normally, use the headlight leveling switch in the level 0 position.

An auto leveling function (static control), which adjusts the beam axis while the vehicle is stopped, has been provided for the low beam headlights of models with discharge headlights to prevent glare to oncoming and preceding vehicles.
The auto leveling system consists of the headlight leveling computer, height control sensor, headlight leveling actuators, etc.

ENTRY.PTXT: Controls the auto leveling function. Determines the vehicle posture and driving condition based on signals from the height control sensor and combination meter, and controls the headlight leveling actuators. When a system malfunction is detected, outputs a headlight auto leveling warning indicator light illumination request signal to the combination meter.
Drives the low beam headlight up and down according to the control signal from the headlight leveling computer to control the direction of the beam axis.
Illuminates the headlight auto leveling warning indicator light according to the signal from the headlight leveling computer. Outputs the vehicle speed signal to the headlight leveling computer.
Detects the vehicle height and outputs a vehicle height change signal to the headlight leveling computer.

ITEM.PTXT: Changes in vehicle posture due to loading of luggage, etc. are detected by the height control sensor installed on the right side of the rear suspension, and the headlight leveling actuators installed in the headlights are driven according to the change in vehicle posture to keep the headlight beam axis at a constant angle while the vehicle is stopped.

The headlight leveling computer, which controls the auto leveling system, receives the vehicle speed signal and the vehicle height change signal from the height control sensor. Based on these signals, it calculates the change in pitch angle of the vehicle posture and drives the headlight leveling actuators according to the posture of the stopped vehicle to control the headlight beam axis.

ENTRY.PTXT: When the headlights are switched from OFF to ON, the headlight leveling actuators are driven according to the current pitch angle change while the vehicle is stopped.
With the headlights ON, the headlight leveling actuators are driven according to the pitch angle at which a change in vehicle posture is detected.

An automatic light control system has been adopted, which detects the ambient brightness and automatically turns on the taillights and headlights when the light control switch is moved to the AUTO position with the power switch (IG) ON.

ENTRY.PTXT: Driver Side Door Courtesy Light Switch

ITEM.PTXT: The automatic light control system controls turning on/off of the taillights and headlights as shown in the table. The following operations are explained using the No. in the Light Operation List by Automatic Light Control System.

INDICATE.TITLE: Automatic Light Control System Operation List

ITEM.PTXT: When the ambient condition is brighter than the taillight off illuminance and headlight off illuminance, both the taillights and headlights are turned off.

ENTRY.PTXT: When It Momentarily Becomes Dark While the Ambient Condition Is Bright (No.5)

ITEM.PTXT: When the ambient condition changes from headlight off illuminance to on illuminance while it is bright, the taillights illuminate because the taillight on illuminance has already been reached, but the headlights do not illuminate. If it is still darker than the on illuminance after the delay time has elapsed, the headlights illuminate; if it is brighter than the on illuminance after the delay time has elapsed, the headlights remain off, which prevents momentary headlight illumination when it becomes momentarily dark while passing under an overpass or along a tree-lined road in bright conditions. However, if it becomes as dark as the headlight rapid-on illuminance, the headlights illuminate.

ENTRY.PTXT: When Ambient Condition Is Dim, Dark or Momentarily Bright (No.6 to No.8)

ITEM.PTXT: When the ambient condition is dim and becomes darker than the taillight on illuminance, the taillights illuminate. (No.6)
When it becomes even darker than the headlight on illuminance, the headlights also illuminate. (No.7)
Even if the ambient condition momentarily becomes bright due to street lights, etc. while the headlights are illuminated, the headlights do not turn off. (No.8)

ENTRY.PTXT: When Power Switch (IG) Is Turned OFF (No.9)

ITEM.PTXT: When the power switch (IG) is turned OFF from the above state (No.6 to No.8), both the taillights and headlights remain illuminated. If the light control switch is then turned OFF once and set to AUTO again from this state, both the taillights and headlights turn off.

ENTRY.PTXT: When the Power Switch (IG) Is Turned OFF and the Driver Side Door Is Opened, and Then Closed (No.10, No.11)

ITEM.PTXT: When the driver side door is opened (driver side door courtesy light switch ON) from the above state (No.9), both the taillights and headlights turn off. (No.10)
When the driver side door is closed (driver side door courtesy light switch OFF) from the above state, both the taillights and headlights remain off. (No.11)

ENTRY.PTXT: When the Power Switch (IG) Is Turned ON Again with the Driver Side Door Closed (No.12)

ITEM.PTXT: When the power switch (IG) is turned ON again from the above state (No.10, No.11) and the ambient condition is dark, both the taillights and headlights illuminate.

ENTRY.PTXT: When the Driver Side Door Is Opened Again from the Above State (No.12) (No.13)

ITEM.PTXT: Even if the driver side door is opened again (driver side door courtesy light switch ON) from the above state (No.12), both the taillights and headlights remain illuminated if the ambient condition is dark.

MECA.TITLE: Fail-safe Function of Automatic Light Control System

ITEM.PTXT: When the output frequency from the light control sensor falls below 30Hz, the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly) determines that the light control sensor has failed or that there is an open or short in the wire harness, and performs fail-safe.

If an input malfunction from the light control sensor is detected when the light control switch is in the AUTO position and the power switch (IG) is ON, and the headlights and taillights are illuminated, the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly) keeps them illuminated until the headlights and taillights are turned OFF by the light auto turn off system or the light control switch is turned OFF. If the headlights and taillights are off, control by the automatic light control system is not performed and they remain off. If the output frequency from the light control sensor returns to normal during fail-safe, control by the automatic light control system automatically resumes.

Detects the illuminance around the vehicle with the scanner section (integrated optical sensor) and outputs it as a frequency signal to the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly). It is installed on the right side of the upper part of the instrument panel.

The circuit that controls the system is built into the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly).

MECA.TITLE: Light Auto Turn Off System Function

ITEM.PTXT: When the power switch is turned OFF and the driver side door is opened while the headlights or taillights (including front fog lights and rear fog light) are illuminated with the power switch (IG) ON and the light control switch (HEAD or TAIL) ON or in the AUTO position, the headlights and taillights are automatically turned off.
Even if the driver side door is opened with the power switch (IG) ON and then the power switch is turned OFF, the headlights and taillights are automatically turned off.
After automatic turn off, the light auto turn off system can be canceled by moving the light control switch from a position other than OFF to OFF, or by turning the power switch (IG) ON.
If a flashing operation is performed during automatic turn off, the headlights illuminate but the light auto turn off system is not canceled.

ENTRY.PTXT: When the light control switch is turned ON with the power switch (IG) ON.

As a result, the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly) outputs the taillight ON signal and, when the headlight switch is ON, drives the headlight relay.
When the power switch (IG) is turned OFF and the driver side door is opened from the normal illumination operation state.

When the power switch (IG) is turned OFF from the above normal illumination operation state, the main body ECU (instrument panel junction block assembly) keeps each light illuminated.
